Program introduction: Interesting stories and experiences about “National Palace”, the essence of K-culture that Koreans don’t know about
Other contents: What is National Palace? Even though we are an archery powerhouse that has won four gold medals in women's archery, Koreans do not know our archery (national archery). At a time when Western bows were only increasing in size with simple bows to become stronger, our ancestors mixed more than 10 different materials to make hapbows. It is small in size and the distance the arrow flies is much more than twice that of Western bows. It is worth inferring why medieval knights began wearing helmets and armor despite their poor combat power. Korean bows were small and easy to carry, so it was also very easy to ambush them with a bow. The power of the small arrow flew very far and strong, and there was enough time to fire several arrows before the Westerner could draw the string of the large simple bow.

Program introduction: Part 1 Program <Open Mic> &<Common Ground> (15:00-16:50) A stage where jazz jam sessions and improvisations are performed in which citizens participate. It is an open performance where not only those who apply in advance but also anyone present can freely go on stage and play and enjoy together. ‘Open Mic’, which has received a warm response and love from citizens for many years, provides an unforgettable special moment where you can fully experience the value of jazz improvisation and communication. A stage where the powerful energy of SNL Korea house band ‘Common Round’ stands out. Korean traditional music and jazz meet to create an exciting collaborative performance, and traditional music is reinterpreted with the sensibility of jazz to capture the unique satire and humor of Korean traditional music. This performance, which combines exciting melodies and colorful performances, will transform Nodeul Island into a special space where Korean traditional music and jazz harmonize. Part 2 Program <Seoul Jazz Friends>&<Nandang Project> 18:00-21:00 This is a stage planned in line with the purpose of the Seoul Jazz Festa, which aims to be an eco-friendly festival. Through jazz, it illuminates the common challenges of humanity such as climate crisis, ecosystem change, war, refugees, and hunger issues. It will be a meaningful stage that delivers a message about a sustainable future through music and emphasizes the power of love and empathy that jazz has. A total arts stage that reinterprets the excitement and dynamism of traditional Korean marketplaces in a modern way. It presents a creative fusion performance combining Korean traditional music, jazz, hip-hop, and modern dance. Jazz diva Woongsan, pansori master Lee Bong-geun, rapper MC Sniper, and modern dancer Iruda join in to produce an original performance. The ‘Nanjang Project’ harmonizes the sensibilities of traditional music and jazz to create a flexible coexistence that transcends genres. This stage, where tradition and the present coexist, presents a new global music trend that expands beyond Korea and into the world.

Performer information: Seongjae Choi (b. 1962) majored in ceramics at the Department of Crafts and Graduate School of Hongik University College of Fine Arts. He has received major awards including the Grand Prize at the 2nd International Ceramic Art Exhibition (1996) and the Grand Prize at the Gyeonggi Province Art Exhibition (2001). He participated in many special exhibitions of major public institutions such as the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, the Seoul Museum of Art, and the Gyeonggi Ceramic Museum, and introduced them at international events such as the Gyeonggi International Ceramic Biennale and the Cheongju Craft Biennale, widely publicizing the modern potential of Korean ceramics. In particular, it has proven its international scope of activity by participating in invitation exhibitions from leading overseas institutions such as the Kyushu Ceramic Art Museum in Japan, Jingdezhen Ceramic University in China, and Alfred University in the United States. Starting with his first overseas exhibition at the Banff Arts Center in Canada in the early 1990s, his work, which has continued for over 30 years, is evaluated as a harmonious fusion of tradition and modernity. His works are collected in leading domestic and international institutions, including the Philadelphia Museum of Art in the United States, the Victoria and Albert Museum in the United Kingdom, the National Ceramic Art Museum in Sèvres in France, the Yongchuan Celadon Museum in China, the Asian Ceramic Art Museum, the National Gallery of Victoria in Australia, the Museu Del Cantir Argentona in Barcelona, Spain, the Horim Museum, and the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art. He is currently serving as a professor in the Department of Traditional Arts and Crafts at Korea University of Cultural Heritage.
Program introduction: Gallery Jiuheon opens the solo exhibition “A Momentary Body Stroke: Landscapes Drawn by the Heart” by Seongjae Choi, who represents the experimental spirit of the Korean ceramic art world. This exhibition is the artist's first solo exhibition in Seoul in six years, and its depth is revealed through 28 carefully selected works representing the artist's 38-year artistic journey of harmony between traditional techniques and modern painting language.

Performer information: PROFILE PIANO BOULEVARD The two pianists, whose musical inclinations blend well together, are founding members of ‘Piano Boulevard,’ Korea’s first piano ensemble group formed in 2013 by music director Lim Mi-jeong and six pianists. Kyung-Hwa Lee is active as General Director of Piano Boulevard, and Yeon-Kyung Jo is active as Project Director. Piano Boulevard, which is showing a new area for piano ensembles by presenting experimental explorations of classical piano ensembles and high-quality duo works, received great response from the children's performances ‘Baby Elephant Baba's Story’ and ‘Piano Meets Movies’, and sold out all tickets and toured the country. Their relationship, which respects each other's music and is solidifying its position as a duo, began while working together on a doctoral course at Hansei University. Lee Kyung-hwa published "A Comparative Analysis Study on J.M. Kraus's Clavier Sonata VB195&196" and Jo Yeon-kyung published "A Study on William Gillock's Romantic Style Preludes for Intermediate Learners" as her doctoral thesis. 주목을 받은 바 있다. At the invitation of Pianoteacher.com, the Duo Recital was held three times in Washington D.C. and Manhattan, New York, and received favorable reviews from American audiences. In Korea, at the invitation of the Praum Musical Instrument Museum, we performed two duo recitals at the Praum Musical Instrument Museum Concert Hall, and performed in a familiar program for citizens with electonist Kim Ho-yeon at the Seoul Arts Center's outdoor festival SAC Festa. In addition, K3PA (Korean Piano Performance and Teaching Association) presented duo works by composer Minji Kim and performed several duo performances. PIANIST KYUNG HWA LEE Kyung-Hwa Lee After graduating from Yewon School, Kyung-Hwa Lee became the youngest person to be admitted to the Vienna University of Music in Austria. Afterwards, he graduated from the Mozarteum Master School in Salzburg, Austria, and earned a doctorate in piano performance from Hansei University Graduate School. He won first place in the Chosun Ilbo and Music Spring and Autumn Competitions and participated in many international competitions and music festivals, including third place in the Padova in Italien International Competition, showing his outstanding musicianship. Also, as the last student of Hans Leygraf, he participated as a producer and performer in the DVD ‘Fundamental piano lessons’. After returning to Korea, he held several recitals at the Sejong Center for the Performing Arts and the Seoul Arts Center, starting with a recital at the Kumho Art Hall. He has lectured at Kangwon National University, Kaywon Arts Middle School, Kaywon Arts High School, and Gyeonggi Arts High School, and served as director of the Hansae Center for Harmony at the Music Foundation for Hana and a researcher at the Glocal Culture Cooperation Center under the Hansae University Industry-Academic Cooperation Foundation, and is currently nurturing younger students at Hansae University. PIANIST YEON KYUNG CHO After graduating from Busan Arts High School, Yeon-Kyung Cho earned her bachelor's degree from Kyunghee University and her master's degree from the same graduate school with a full scholarship. Afterwards, he obtained a doctorate in piano teaching from Hansei University Graduate School, and while training younger students at Hansae University and Busan High School of the Arts, he is also actively working as a music educator as the representative of Piano Boulevard Music School. In 2018, a meaningful program dedicated to Korean War veterans was presented at a recital held in Chicago, USA at the invitation of the Korean Council for Reconciliation and Cooperation and at the ‘Korean War Armistice 65th Anniversary Commemoration Event’ at Daly Square in front of Chicago City Hall, and an encore recital at the Chamber Hall of the Busan Cultural Center and a recital at the Sejong Center for the Performing Arts were held. After being invited to perform at the Vietnam National University of Music located in Hanoi, he appeared at the ‘Korea-Vietnam 25th Anniversary Concert of Diplomatic Relations in Seoul’ and the ‘Jeju International Music Festival’ held at the Seoul Arts Center, and participated as a lecturer and performer in the music education program <Music Education for ALL> held at the National University of Arts and Culture in Yangon, Myanmar. In addition, he served as the exclusive pianist at the Seoul Arts Center Outdoor Festival (SAC Festa) and as a volunteer program coordinator for the performance business team of the Music Foundation for Hana, and is currently serving as the chairman of the board of directors of Shine J Art & Music, an incorporated organization.
